title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, reconstructed from the previous and next pages. X is a surface (eventually a compact, differentiable, orientable one) with a finite set I of marked points. G is a topological group acting on (X,S). The previous page gave a canonical extension G~ of G by Z^I = T_I, obtained by pulling back an extension T~ = 'Sp T' of the Teichmüller-type group T = pi_0(A) by Z^I along G -> T (diagram 141). The previous page calls this the 'special Teichmüller group' of (X,S).

On this page X has some extra structure (analytic or differentiable) near I. For each x in I:
- D_x^* is a punctured disc neighbourhood of x.
- S_x is the associated circle at x: the boundary circle of the real oriented blow-up, i.e. the circle of tangent directions, onto which D_x^* retracts.
- S~_x is 'the' universal cover of S_x (a copy of R), chosen compatibly with the universal cover D_x^{*~} of D_x^*.

Formula (142) sets S~_I = disjoint union over x in I of S~_x. This is a T_I-torsor over S_I = union of the S_x, with T_I = Z^I acting by deck translations.

Claim. For u in G (which may permute I), there is a bijection between two sets of lifts:
- lifts u~ of u|D_I^* to an automorphism of the universal cover D_I^{*~};
- lifts u~_{S_I} of u|S_I to automorphisms of S~_I that are isomorphisms of T_I-torsors.
This holds because D_x^* is homotopy equivalent to S_x, as a collar S_x x (0,1), given that u respects that structure near I. The bijection is compatible with composition.

Formula (143) follows: G~ is canonically isomorphic to the group of pairs (u, u~_S), with u in G and u~_S a torsor-compatible lift of u|S_I to S~_I. This is the boundary-circle description of the extension of G by Z^I. Its kernel over G is Z^I, the deck translations, which correspond to Dehn twists around the punctures.

Topology. The garbled sentence presumably says that this identification is a homeomorphism when the group of pairs carries the coarsest topology making continuous:
- p_1: G~ -> G;
- q_1: G~ -> Aut top(S~_I), (u, u~_S) |-> u~_S;
- possibly q_1' = q_1∘σ, for some auxiliary map σ that is not defined on this page.
The next page specifies the compact-open topology on Autext(S~_I).

Purpose. This gives a concrete model of the extension of the mapping class group by Z^I (the 'special Teichmüller group' SΓ -> Γ). On the next page it is used to identify such extensions, for compact orientable surfaces, as pullbacks of SΓ -> Γ along G -> Γ. In modern terms this is the mapping class group of a surface with boundary circles, or framed / tangentially-based mapping class group: a central extension of Γ_{g,n} by Z^n generated by boundary twists. Grothendieck realises it via lifts to the universal cover of the circles of directions, which is the topological shadow of tangential base points.
errors: Lifts of a circle homeomorphism to R commute with deck translations only if the map preserves orientation. Orientation-reversing elements anti-commute, so 'isomorphism of T_I-torsors' must be read as semilinear (twisted by the sign), or G must be orientation-preserving near I. This is not stated on the page.
The bijection between lifts on D_I^* and on S_I tacitly assumes that u respects the collar/product structure near I, or is isotopic to such a map; otherwise one needs a homotopy argument.
The map σ in q_1' = q_1∘σ is not defined on this page; its role (involution or section?) is unclear.

ideas.what: Extension of a group of surface homeomorphisms by Z^I, realised as pairs (u, lift of u to the universal cover of the boundary/direction circles at the punctures)
ideas.modern_name: mapping class group of surface with boundary as central extension of Γ_{g,n} by Z^n (boundary Dehn twists); framed / tangential mapping class group
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Birman, Harer, etc.); tangential base points: Deligne 1989
ideas.where_published: Teichmüller groups and their extensions appear in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche; this specific boundary-lift model is unsure

ideas.what: Topology on the extension group as the coarsest topology making the projection and the lift-action on S~_I (compact-open) continuous
ideas.modern_name: initial topology / compact-open topology on homeomorphism groups

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard topological model of the Z^I extension of the mapping class group (boundary twists / tangential framings). It is well known today, and the page contains no new result or unexplored connection.
transcription_corrections: In (143) and the preceding text, 'rel. de u_{S_I} au rev. univ. de S~_I' should read roughly 'relèvement de u_{S_I} en un automorphisme de S~_I'; similarly 'reliements ũ_{D_I^*} … au rev. univ. D_I^{*~}' means lifts to an automorphism of D_I^{*~}.

The sentence 'On vérifie que l'on a un homéom. top. sur ce dernier [?] … la top. la moins fine' is barely legible. It likely means: the isomorphism (143) is a homeomorphism when the right-hand group carries the coarsest topology making the maps (144) continuous.
Page number 787 is at the top; 278 is the archive folio.
